name: Shen Yulan
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder and actual controller (with father Shen Jiansheng) of Yinbang Clad Material Co. (SZSE: 300337); not a listed executive
profile: Shen Yulan (b. 1988) is the son of Yinbang founder/chairman Shen Jiansheng; father and son jointly control Wuxi-based Yinbang Clad Material, a maker of aluminium-alloy clad strip and foil for brazed heat exchangers (auto, HVAC, power). The pair held ~80% pre-IPO before the 2012 ChiNext listing; a May 2026 filing still names him a controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Yinbang developed its own brazing aluminium-alloy clad plate/strip/foil in 2005, the core product behind its growth supplying heat-exchanger makers.
deep_cut_fact: He was listed first among the 45 individual founding promoters when Yinbang was converted into a joint-stock company on 8 Dec 2010, when he was about 22.
notes: Low public profile; father Shen Jiansheng is chairman and the public face. IR email is from the 2012 prospectus; confirm in the latest annual report. Best route is via the company securities office.

name: Corinne Flick
current_role: Founder and head of the Convoco Foundation (think tank, Berlin/London/Salzburg); general partner of Vivil GmbH & Co. KG, Offenburg
profile: Dr Corinne Michaela Flick, a lawyer trained at LMU Munich (doctorate 1989), is married to Gert-Rudolf Flick of the Flick industrial dynasty and comes from the family behind Vivil confectionery. She founded the interdisciplinary think tank Convoco in 2004, runs its Salzburg forum, London/Berlin lectures, podcast and the Convoco Edition book series.
interesting_fact: Before founding Convoco she worked as a lawyer at Bertelsmann Buch AG in London and at Amazon.com in Munich; she has also been a general partner of Vivil (Offenburg) since 1998.
deep_cut_fact: The Jewish Museum Berlin gave her its Prize for Understanding and Tolerance (alongside Wolfgang Ischinger); the jury noted that every Convoco topic takes the German Basic Law as its reference point.
notes: Wealth is via the Flick family (husband Gert-Rudolf Flick) and Vivil. Very relevant fit: she hosts a think-tank podcast and her council includes energy-sector figures; approach via Convoco's general inbox.

name: Dmitriy Zaporozhets
current_role: GitLab co-founder; left his Engineering Fellow role in Nov 2021; describes himself as a software developer (no confirmed current executive role)
profile: Kharkiv-born engineer who wrote the first version of GitLab in October 2011 as an open-source, self-hostable GitHub alternative with Valery Sizov, then co-founded GitLab Inc. with Sid Sijbrandij (CTO, later Engineering Fellow). He rang the Nasdaq bell at the October 2021 IPO and stepped away a month later, having fulfilled his 10-year commitment.
interesting_fact: The GitLab name was an accident: he and Valery Sizov were hunting for a cheap short 'git' domain and found gitlabhq.com for sale for $12.
deep_cut_fact: He studied computer-aided diagnosis of motor vehicles at Kharkiv National Automobile and Highway University, hoping to design cars, and taught himself C by writing a clone of two levels of Mario for Windows.
notes: Low-key engineer, not a media personality; he publishes his own email on his personal site, so a direct, technical note is the best route. Spells his name Dmytro in recent profiles.

name: Qiao Tianming
current_role: Former chairman of Sichuan Jiannanchun (JNC) Group, the Mianzhu baijiu maker; no active public role since c.2016
profile: Qiao Tianming spent more than 30 years at Jiannanchun, one of the 'Mao-Wu-Jian' baijiu brands. He became chairman in 2001 and led its 2003 restructuring from state ownership, which made him a major owner. He largely vanished from public view around 2016, and in 2023 a Leshan court convicted him in a case tied to that restructuring.
interesting_fact: In 2012 he announced the RMB 2bn Datang Guojiu eco-park to add 20,000+ tonnes of base-liquor capacity; it was only formally unveiled in 2022, a decade later.
notes: Not a viable podcast guest. He was reported missing from public view around 2016, and in 2023 the Leshan Intermediate Court sentenced him to 5 years for bribery and illegally dividing state assets, with a RMB 400m fine (per media reports). Some reports say his son Qiao Yu took on management. Source: https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2018-07-24/1238247.html and tmtpost.

name: Wang Chunming
current_role: Founder/controller of Sichuan Guodong Construction Group (Chengdu); former chairman of Guodong Construction (SSE: 600321, now Zhengyuan Co.)
profile: Wang Chunming built Chengdu-based Sichuan Guodong Construction Group and was legal representative and chairman of its listed arm, Sichuan Guodong Construction Co., which IPO'd in Shanghai in 2001. In 2016 Guodong Group agreed to sell control (about RMB 2.5bn at RMB 7/share) to Zhengyuan Real Estate (Fu Yanbin). Guodong Group and an affiliate still held ~22.9% in 2023 as second-largest holder.
interesting_fact: Guodong Construction's March 2001 Shanghai IPO sold 70m shares at RMB 12.28 each (about 28x earnings), lifting its share capital from 105.2m to 175.2m shares.
notes: Very low public profile and little personal coverage; no published personal or office contact found. Control sale source: https://stock.stockstar.com/SS2016101100001192.shtml; 2023 stake: https://paper.cnstock.com/html/2023-04/10/content_1746133.htm. Not an obvious podcast fit.

name: Rohan Murthy
current_role: Founder of Soroco (AI work-graph/Scout platform) and Workfabric AI (Context Fabric); founder of the Murty Classical Library of India
profile: Rohan Murty (usually spelled Murty) is the son of Infosys co-founder N. R. Narayana Murthy and author Sudha Murty and an Infosys shareholder. He earned a Harvard PhD in computer science (2011), then founded Soroco, whose Scout platform maps how office work flows, and later Workfabric AI, which grounds AI agents in an organisation's own work context; Cognizant is a client.
interesting_fact: He funded the Murty Classical Library of India with a $5.2m gift (2010); published by Harvard University Press, it was set to reach 50 bilingual volumes from 14 languages spanning 25 centuries by end-2025.
deep_cut_fact: He was sure by sixth or seventh grade he'd be a professor, as teaching is the 'family business': six or seven generations on his mother's side and four on his father's were teachers. His father talked to him about Alan Turing and George Boole.
notes: Spells surname 'Murty'. Strong fit for an AI/data podcast. Co-founder of both companies is George Nychis. Best route: Workfabric AI's general inbox or Soroco contact form.

name: Chen Desong
current_role: Former chairman and actual controller of Chunghsin Technology Group (Zhongxin Keji, SSE: 603996), Taizhou, Zhejiang; no longer controller
profile: Chen Desong co-founded Chunghsin Technology in Taizhou, Zhejiang (2007, with Jiang Zhenhui), an electronics ODM making flat-panel TVs, notebooks, tablets and phones that listed in Shanghai in 2015. He was chairman and legal representative, but the group's parent, Chunghsin Industry Group, later went into bankruptcy liquidation, and regulators named him the 'former actual controller' in 2023.
interesting_fact: Chunghsin grew from a 2007 Taizhou start-up into a Shanghai-listed contract manufacturer of TVs, notebooks, tablets and phones within about eight years.
notes: Not recommended for outreach. A 2023 filing says the CSRC warned and fined former controllers Chen Desong and Jiang Zhenhui RMB 1.6m each and imposed 10-year securities-market bans over undisclosed related-party fund occupation (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202311171611365228_1.pdf). The parent group was ordered into bankruptcy liquidation (2021). Wealth figure is likely obsolete.

name: Tim Martin
current_role: Founder and chairman, J D Wetherspoon plc
profile: Sir Tim Martin (b. 1955, Norwich) is a Nottingham law graduate who qualified as a barrister in 1979 but never practised; he bought his first pub in Muswell Hill that year and built J D Wetherspoon into a chain of 800+ UK and Ireland pubs (listed 1992). He still chairs it and owned ~24% of the shares as of 2023; outspoken Brexit backer and campaigner for pub/supermarket tax parity.
interesting_fact: Wetherspoon is named after one of his teachers, who could not control his class; the first pub was originally called Martin's Free House.
deep_cut_fact: Son of an RAF officer turned Guinness marketing executive, he attended eleven schools in New Zealand and Northern Ireland, including Campbell College, Belfast, and his early jobs included labouring on a building site in Ware and selling for The Times.
notes: Very media-accessible and opinionated; regularly does interviews (e.g. Shares magazine 2024: https://sharesmagazine.co.uk/article/discover-how-tim-martin-turned-wetherspoon-into-a-high-street-champion). Best route is the Wetherspoon press office; its site blocked automated fetches and the search budget ran out before a published press email could be confirmed.

name: Liu Shiqiang
current_role: Individual shareholder of Yonyou Network Technology (SSE: 600588); no executive role found
profile: A Liu Shiqiang appears among Yonyou Network's top-ten shareholders as a domestic individual: 68m shares (1.98%) in an April 2022 disclosure, falling to about 32m shares (0.94%) by Sept 2026. No biography, executive role or other public profile was found, so who he is beyond being a shareholder is unconfirmed.
interesting_fact: He has been one of Yonyou's largest individual shareholders, holding about 2% of the enterprise-software company in 2022.
notes: Appears to be a private (possibly financial) investor rather than a founder or executive. Holding trend from https://quote.cfi.cn/gdtj/1296/600588.html. Not a named Yonyou executive; there is no outreach route other than the company IR. Name is also shared with an unrelated Jiangxi Agricultural University professor.

name: Lai Zhenyuan
current_role: Founder and long-time chairman of Longyuan Construction Group (SSE: 600491); his family remains a major shareholder (current board title unverified)
profile: Lai Zhenyuan rose through Xiangshan No.2 Construction (Ningbo), becoming general manager in 1993, then chairman after its 1995 restructuring, and chairman of the renamed Longyuan Construction from 1996. In 2023 the Lai family agreed to cede control to state-owned Hangzhou Communications Investment Group via share sale plus private placement, but the plan was terminated in April 2026.
interesting_fact: He ran Xiangshan No.2 Construction's Shanghai branch from 1984 to 1993, the foothold from which Longyuan became a major Shanghai contractor with 300+ quality awards, including Luban Prizes.
deep_cut_fact: He has been named a Zhejiang Province model worker and a national outstanding construction entrepreneur, and served as vice-chairman of the Shanghai Construction Industry Association.
notes: Control-transfer termination announcement: https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202604301821855051_1.pdf. Bio page is an older profile, so verify current board roles in the latest annual report. No published personal or office contact found; the route would be the company securities office.

name: Liu Zhaonian
current_role: Founder and vice-chairman, Jointown Pharmaceutical Group (SSE: 600998), Wuhan
profile: Liu Zhaonian (name listed as 'Liu Zhaonain') co-founded Jointown with his brothers Liu Baolin and Liu Shulin, building one of China's largest pharmaceutical distributors (listed in Shanghai 2010; 2025 revenue RMB 161.4bn). As vice-chairman he still speaks at its shareholder meetings, most recently in May 2026, on pharmacy-channel strategy.
interesting_fact: At Jointown's May 2026 AGM he called the shift of prescriptions from hospitals to retail pharmacies 'irreversible'; its Haoyaoshi franchise network already exceeds 34,500 stores and 60m members.
notes: Brother relationship and shareholding per 2015 annual report summary: https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN201504270009386215_1.pdf. Older filings list only individual staff mailboxes, so they are not included. Best route is Jointown's board secretary / IR office. Good fit for a healthcare-logistics angle.

name: ZhaoMin
current_role: Vice-chairman and general manager, Wuxi New Hongtai Electrical Technology Co. (SSE: 603016)
profile: Zhao Minhai (趙敏海, listed as 'ZhaoMin'; b. 1979, Tsinghua EMBA) built Wuxi New Hongtai with his family (co-listed holder Zhao Hanxin). It makes circuit-breaker key components, low-voltage breakers and BMC/SMC moulded insulation parts. He was chairman 2016-2023; after state-owned Wuxi Industry Development Group took control in 2023 he stayed on as vice-chairman and GM, holding ~26m shares.
interesting_fact: New Hongtai is a grid-equipment play: it supplies moulded-case and air circuit breakers, moulded insulation parts and breaker motor-operating mechanisms, and is classed under power equipment / grid equipment.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the family business at about 23, in October 2002, and was already vice-chairman and general manager by 2008, before the company's IPO.
notes: Name in source data is truncated ('ZhaoMin'); the Chinese name 赵敏海 matches the New Hongtai executive. Relevant to an energy/grid-equipment angle. Route via the company board secretary's office (Du Jianping per 10jqka).

name: Wang Yuxiang
current_role: Chairman (and acting CFO), PIESAT Information Technology (SSE STAR: 688066); Beijing CPPCC member
profile: Wang Yuxiang (b. 1975) holds a PhD in cartography and GIS from the CAS Institute of Remote Sensing and Digital Earth. He co-founded Beijing remote-sensing software and services firm PIESAT in 2008 and controls it with co-founder Zhang Yan. PIESAT now builds its own 'Nuwa' satellite constellation. Note: it reported a 2025 net loss of RMB 1.86bn with overdue debts and going-concern doubts.
interesting_fact: At the January 2026 Beijing 'two sessions' he proposed a 'space data centre innovation consortium' to crack power supply, cooling and inter-satellite links for orbital computing; PIESAT's Nuwa compute satellites target ~4 PFLOPS per satellite in dawn-dusk orbit.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding PIESAT he was technical director at Beijing Nova Information Technology, part of Finland's Novo Group (2002-04), then at Founder-Aode (2004-08); he is on China's national 'Ten Thousand Talents' programme.
notes: Excellent fit for a data-centre/energy podcast (space computing, orbital data centres). Caveat: PIESAT is in financial distress (2025 loss, debt overdue; an independent director abstained on the Q1 2026 report citing going-concern doubt, per CS.com.cn filings). Route via the board secretary's office.

name: Zheng Chunlan
current_role: Co-actual controller and top-ten shareholder of Petpal Pet Nutrition Technology (SZSE: 300673), with husband and chairman Chen Zhenbiao; no executive title found
profile: Zheng Xianglan (郑香兰; listed as 'Zheng Chunlan') and her husband Chen Zhenbiao jointly control Petpal, a Pingyang, Wenzhou maker of dog chews and pet treats. Petpal listed in Shenzhen in July 2017 as China's 'first pet-food stock'. She remained a top-ten holder and co-controller as of the Q3 2025 report.
interesting_fact: Petpal grew out of Shuitou town's leather industry: leather offcuts became raw material for dog chews in the early 1990s, and chews were over 90% of Petpal's sales in 2014-2016.
notes: English name in source data appears to be a mistransliteration of 郑香兰 (Zheng Xianglan). Low profile; husband Chen Zhenbiao (a former Wenzhou middle-school teacher who started in pet chews in 1992) is the public face. Controller status: https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2025-10-28/1224742716.PDF. Route via the company securities office.

name: Hao Jiangbo
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List (2016-2019) with source of wealth 'Youzi' (Investments). Searches in Chinese and English found no verifiable public record linking a Hao Jiangbo (郝江波) to a named company, fund or listed-company shareholding, so identity could not be confirmed.
notes: 'Youzi' (游资) is the Chinese term for 'hot money' short-term traders, so he may be a private stock trader rather than a company founder; this is unverified. Too little public information; deprioritise.
